title: A keyboard that changed my workflow
description: My hands-on thoughts on the CLVX 1, a keyboard with a touchpad built into the keys.
paragraphs: Just upgraded to the CLVX 1 Keyboard by Clevetura — and it’s hands-down the best I’ve tried (and I’ve tried a lot).

Working across code, docs, design tools, and more, I switch between mouse and keyboard constantly. I’ve owned countless peripherals—mechanical, ergonomic, low-profile—but nothing has had me this impressed.

This is a total game-changer. The capacitive layer on the alpha keys doubles as a trackpad, automatically switching between typing and touch modes. Cursor control, gestures, scrolling—it all happens right on the keys. No reaching for the mouse. It’s intuitive, lightning-fast, and surprisingly precise.

No hot-swappables here—the keys use scissor-mechanical switches with 1.2 mm travel and ~60 g actuation. Crisp and quiet, perfect for long typing sessions. They’re solid—rated for 3 million keystrokes.
Anodized aluminum base. Polycarbonate top. 110-key full ANSI layout with low profile (~12.4 mm thick) and just 640 g weight. This thing is both elegant and durable.

131 RGB LEDs with gesture-following lighting. Auto-brightness adjusts to ambient light. There are also touch sliders across the function row you can use for volume, brightness—or remap them via the app.
USB-C wired plus three Bluetooth 5.1 channels. Quickly toggle between desktop, laptop, tablet—effortless multi-device workflow.
Workflow flow: Being able to scroll, click, and drag without moving hands off the keyboard—massive streamlining.
Muscle memory: A slight adjustment period, but shifting to trackpad mode is seamless. You’ll forget what missing a mouse feels like.
Personalized control: Between KeyTap, Type button, left/right-click buttons under the spacebar, and sensitivity toggles—this thing adapts to your preferences and hand usage.
Battery lasts ~80 hrs without backlight—it depletes faster with RGB on (1-1.5d with 100% brightness).

A high-end, full-sized keyboard that integrates a touchpad into the typing surface itself—no compromises. Built-quality, wireless flexibility, full gesture support—without mechanical key switches or separate touchpad. If you’re after a cleaner desk and smoother navigation, this is a serious upgrade.
Huge thanks to the Clevetura team for redefining what a modern keyboard can be.
I'd love to hear from you: what keyboard/trackpad combo are you using? Have you tried integrated touch surfaces yet?
